content:
maria_oncall: Heads-up — p99 for text-gen-v2 in eu-west-1 jumped to ~4.8s starting ~02:10 UTC. Multiple support tickets referencing timeouts. p95 up to ~650ms. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd1234/text-gen-metrics :rotating_light:
ben_sre: On it. Can you paste the exact dashboard panel link and any recent deploys or routing changes?
maria_oncall: Panel: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd1234/p99-panel. We did a canary routing change at 01:55 that shifted ~15% to gpu-pool-b for text-gen-v2 (weight-based routing rollout). No code deploys to model code itself.
emily_platform: Pulling autoscaler and queue metrics now — looking at instance churn and queue depth.
ops-bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected for service/text-gen-v2 (eu-west-1). threshold=900ms, observed=4800ms. Incident score=medium-high.
charlie_runtime: Observing a spike in KV cache misses and cold-start latency on nodes in gpu-pool-b. Heap/GC not obvious, but kernel selection differences on the new pool cause a larger working set -> eviction -> cache miss storm.
ben_sre: Triage + mitigations suggestion (short order):
  1) enable model fallback in eu-west-1 for latency-sensitive routes to text-gen-v2-quant (lower mem, faster tail).
  2) set an aggressive circuit breaker for public /v1/generate traffic to protect p95 during remediation.
  3) roll back canary routing to previous weights while we investigate.
maria_oncall: +1. How do we enable fallback quickly? Need exact command to run in region scope.
ben_sre: Use the CLI snippet below to set region-scoped route fallback:
```
# enable model fallback for route /v1/generate in eu-west-1
redwood-cli routes set-fallback --region eu-west-1 --route "/v1/generate" --fallback-model text-gen-v2-quant --priority 10
```
emily_platform: Then set a short-window circuit breaker (soft-fail) so we shed excess tail requests:
```
# soft CB to protect latency SLO
redwood-cli runtime circuit-breaker set --service text-gen-v2 --region eu-west-1 --window 60s --failure-threshold 0.8 --action reject
```
charlie_runtime: Also recommend warming top prefixes into KV cache for 30m and limiting streaming chunk size for that pool — reduces working set spike. I can run a warmup job for top-100 prefixes.
maria_oncall: I'm executing the fallback and CB now, will post updates. Pinging support lead.
ops-bot: ACTION: fallback enabled, circuit breaker applied, canary rollback queued (initiated by ben_sre).
emily_platform: Seeing p99 drop to ~1.1s after fallback + CB, p95 back under 400ms. Still above ideal SLO (p99 target 900ms). Keep monitoring for 10m.
charlie_runtime: I'm kicking off the cache-warmup job and a scaled repro load against gpu-pool-b to validate tail behavior:
```
# quick repro load (non-prod token)
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN" -d '{"model":"text-gen-v2","input":"hello"}' & done
```
ben_sre: Rolling back canary weights to previous configuration (reducing traffic to gpu-pool-b) — will monitor.
maria_oncall: Updating tickets and support threads with mitigation steps and ETA. Creating follow-up: post-incident doc + action items. Assigning charlie_runtime to investigate kernel/selection variance and cache eviction pattern. Assigning ben_sre to harden routing rollout guardrails (automatic rollback threshold if p99 > 2x baseline). ETA 24h. :white_check_mark:
emily_platform: Next steps for follow-up: add an automated SLO guard that triggers fallback + circuit-breaker when p99 crosses 1.5x baseline for >2min, and add a perf test in canary pipeline that validates tail quantiles under representative prefix loads.
maria_oncall: Thanks team — leaving monitoring on. If p99 < 1s in 15m we'll close this thread and move to post-incident writeup.
slo-bot: NOTE: SLO breach recorded for text-gen-v2 in eu-west-1 at 02:10 UTC (p99>900ms). Incident ticket #INC-2024-578 created and linked.
